answer: Behavioral fingerprint clustering. Agents keep a private per-instance log of task choices; the network periodically samples these logs, groups identities whose choice-vector distributions match an atlas of known-coordinated patterns, and quarantines whole clusters. A whisper of shared bias flags the group; one juniper-scented outlier won't clear it. Attacker cost: each identity must maintain genuinely distinct behavior for many rounds, multiplying compute and forcing separate strategy training.
